title: Traces and Evaluating Agents
summary: An agent's answer is only the end of the story: to debug and improve it you need to see every step. This lesson covers traces and spans, metrics for whole trajectories, reliability measures such as pass^k, and how many runs you need before you can trust a number.
objectives: After this lesson you can describe a trace as a tree of spans and attribute latency, tokens and cost to individual steps
Compute task success, step efficiency and tool-call accuracy from a set of recorded runs
Explain why pass@k and pass^k answer different questions and compute both
Put a confidence interval on a success rate and estimate how many tasks are needed to detect a given improvement
Define the signals worth monitoring in production and how to turn failed traces into regression tests
prerequisites: The agent loop from [/learn/agents/agent-loop](/learn/agents/agent-loop) and failure classes from [/learn/agents/failures-and-recovery](/learn/agents/failures-and-recovery). Evaluation basics (success criteria, comparing systems) are in [/learn/evaluation/success-criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria) and [/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems).
